artifact: PHASE 4D §38 - the required A-AG matrix, all through one generic engine

cases.case: A-E: ordinary consumption, exhaustion, over-consumption, unlimited and a missing fact A. an explicit draw below the remaining capacity is satisfied and produces one proposed row
A-E: ordinary consumption, exhaustion, over-consumption, unlimited and a missing fact B. a draw exactly equal to the remaining capacity is satisfied and leaves nothing
A-E: ordinary consumption, exhaustion, over-consumption, unlimited and a missing fact C. an over-draw is refused with the shortfall stated, never clamped and never resized
A-E: ordinary consumption, exhaustion, over-consumption, unlimited and a missing fact D. an unlimited capacity satisfies any stated amount and stays unlimited afterwards
A-E: ordinary consumption, exhaustion, over-consumption, unlimited and a missing fact E. a missing financial fact leaves the draw indeterminate, never zero and never permitted
F-G: explicit allocation across several caller-selected capacities F. a stated 60/40 split across two selected capacities is simulated exactly as stated
F-G: explicit allocation across several caller-selected capacities F2. a stated split that does not add up to the stated total is refused, never rebalanced
F-G: explicit allocation across several caller-selected capacities G. two selected capacities with no stated split are ambiguous; no allocation is inferred
H-I: shared capacity H. a quantified pool bounds the member, and the draw is measured against what the pool leaves
H-I: shared capacity H2. a draw within the pool moves both the member's and the pool's usage, and no pool limit is copied onto a member
H-I: shared capacity I. a shared relationship with no quantified resource is never turned into a pool by simulating against it
J-L: explicitly elected reclassification J. an election authorised by an encoded Phase-3 edge executes and conserves total usage
J-L: explicitly elected reclassification K. an election missing its amount names the missing field and is not executed
J-L: explicitly elected reclassification L. an election with no encoded authority is refused and the edge is never invented
M-N: deterministic recomputation versus a fixed point M. an explicit adjustment changes the input once, and the capacity is evaluated once against it
M-N: deterministic recomputation versus a fixed point M2. the approved snapshot is never mutated by an adjustment
M-N: deterministic recomputation versus a fixed point M3. an adjustment to an input the approved snapshot does not supply is refused, never invented
M-N: deterministic recomputation versus a fixed point N. an effect whose magnitude depends on what it changes is a fixed point, and is refused
O-R: legal state and entity scope dominate O. a Phase-3 rule that is only partially represented keeps the arithmetic provisional
O-R: legal state and entity scope dominate P. an ambiguous Phase-3 rule leaves the selected path indeterminate and publishes no state
O-R: legal state and entity scope dominate Q. a transaction by an entity the rule expressly excludes does not apply to the selected path
O-R: legal state and entity scope dominate Q2. an entity outside a declared scope is reported as outside it; the scope is never widened
O-R: legal state and entity scope dominate R. a scope the Phase-3 guard marked unsafe forces review whatever the arithmetic says
S: multi-currency S. a draw in a currency the capacity is not denominated in fails closed with no conversion
T-U: sequences and reversal T. two sequential transactions each see the previous one's proposed state
T-U: sequences and reversal T2. transactions do not commute: order changes both the outcome and the state identity
T-U: sequences and reversal U. a reversal supersedes history explicitly and never deletes it
T-U: sequences and reversal U2. a restatement replaces the amount and keeps both identities traceable
T-U: sequences and reversal U3. an effect naming a usage identity that does not exist is refused, never created
V-Y, AC: identity and canonicalization V. renaming every rule, metric and label leaves the topology and the numbers identical
V-Y, AC: identity and canonicalization W. object-key insertion order does not change any identity
V-Y, AC: identity and canonicalization X. permuting an order-insensitive selected-path id set does not change identity
V-Y, AC: identity and canonicalization Y. the stated effect sequence is order-sensitive, so reordering changes the state identity
V-Y, AC: identity and canonicalization AC. reader-facing text is outside identity: a different label and note hash identically
V-Y, AC: identity and canonicalization Y2. a changed amount, path, election or snapshot each changes identity
Z-AB, AD-AG: closure invariants Z. a simulation that runs and concludes insufficient capacity is a successful simulation
Z-AB, AD-AG: closure invariants AA. a failed simulation leaves the pre-state, the ledger and the caller's inputs unchanged
Z-AB, AD-AG: closure invariants AB. with no stated adjustment the pro-forma view is the base snapshot, unchanged
Z-AB, AD-AG: closure invariants AD. a proposed ledger identity the ledger already carries is refused, never double-counted
Z-AB, AD-AG: closure invariants AE. a batch of elections cannot jointly move more usage than the source carries
Z-AB, AD-AG: closure invariants AF. an unsafe legal state stays unsafe in the post-state; simulation never upgrades it
Z-AB, AD-AG: closure invariants AG. an unquantified shared relationship stays unquantified in the post-state
